bib.title: Chapter 5: Extending Your Agent with RAG to Prevent Hallucinations (Building AI Agents with LLMs, RAG, and Knowledge Graphs)

question: How can retrieval-augmented generation give an LLM external, updatable knowledge and reduce hallucinations, and what design choices make up a naive RAG pipeline?
contributions: Explains naive RAG as indexing, retrieval and generation, from TF-IDF/BM25 to dense bi-encoders
Lists design choices for chunking, embedding, vector databases and evaluation
Compares RAG with fine-tuning and builds a movie recommendation agent

limits: No experiments: all claims are explanatory or asserted, with no datasets, baselines or measurements of RAG's effect on hallucination.
Formulas (cosine score, BM25, AP, MRR, quantization) are images and absent from the extracted text.
Demo gives no evaluation, no sampling settings beyond max_new_tokens=800, and the prompt text is truncated in the PDF.
Chapter defers advanced RAG (rerankers, hybrid search, parametric vs context interplay) to the next chapter and concedes the model may still ignore context.
MTEB and vector-DB leaderboards are described as self-reported or generic-domain; leaderboard figures date quickly.
practices: Choose chunk size so it does not exceed the embedder context (truncation loses information); too-small chunks lose context, too-large ones are non-specific and raise inference cost (Chunking strategies).
Use overlap only as a small percentage of chunk size because it grows the database and adds redundancy (Chunking strategies).
Align chunking with document structure, resources, model context limits and expected query patterns; there is no universal best chunker, so evaluate each strategy (Chunking guidelines).
Do not pick an embedder from the MTEB leaderboard alone; test several on your own data because results are self-reported, possibly leaked, and generic-domain (Embedding strategies).
Use the same encoder for query and document embedding at retrieval (Naive RAG, Retrieval step).
Prefer int8 over float32 as a compromise before extreme binary quantization (Embedding strategies).
Use Matryoshka embeddings to truncate vectors with limited loss (Embedding strategies).

Choose a vector database on licence, language support, maturity, insert/query speed, privacy, integration and cost; FAISS suits immutable indexes, not CRUD-heavy systems; SQL vector extensions suit internal projects, dedicated vector DBs suit performance (Embedding databases).
Add related-but-wrong negatives for multiple negatives ranking loss, since random negatives make the task too easy (Embedding strategies).
Evaluate retrieval with precision, recall, MAP and MRR, and generation with LLM-judged faithfulness, context recall/precision and answer relevance (Evaluating the output).

Choose RAG for dynamic data, source tracking and minimal hallucination; fine-tuning for style, skills and specialized domains; combine both, including fine-tuning the embedder, when useful (Comparison between RAG and fine-tuning).
Fine-tune embedders with Sentence Transformers using positive/negative pairs, possibly synthetic LLM-generated (Comparison section).

terms.definition: We define the knowledge from the LLM as parametric memory and that obtained from the RAG as external or nonparametric.
A system of three parts: indexing, retrieval and generation.
A data structure composed of a dictionary and postings, designed to make it efficient to search for terms in a set of documents.
A variant of TF-IDF where two parameters are added: b (document length normalization) and k (relationship between TF and IDF; TF saturation).
One encoder extracts the query representation and another each document/chunk representation; document embeddings are precomputed and compared by cosine similarity.
Split like context-aware chunks, then join chunks up to a predetermined token count.
Divides on atomic self-contained factoids, which an LLM groups by semantic coherence.
Training so the most important information sits in early dimensions, letting vectors be truncated while keeping downstream performance.
Ratio of claims in the generated answer that can be inferred from the context to total claims in the answer.
Average over queries of the reciprocal of the rank of the first relevant item.
A BERT-derived model labels the passage in the text that answers a query, instead of retrieving chunks.
